hook.en: When the owner of a shop takes ₹2,000 from the counter for his son's fees, is it a business expense? The basic concepts answer such questions.

title.en: Business entity, money measurement and going concern

body.en: Business entity: the business is separate from its owner, so the owner's personal transactions are not recorded and capital is treated as a liability to the owner. Money measurement: only transactions that can be expressed in money are recorded. Going concern: the business is assumed to continue for a long time, so assets are shown at cost less depreciation and not at their sale value.
body.kn: ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಘಟಕ: ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಮಾಲೀಕರಿಂದ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ. ಹಣದ ಅಳತೆ: ಹಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಳೆಯಬಹುದಾದವನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ದಾಖಲಿಸುವುದು. ನಡೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ: ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲ ಮುಂದುವರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬ ಊಹೆ.

points.en: Owner's personal expenses: drawings, not business expenses

title.en: Business entity: the owner is separate

narration.en: Under the business entity concept the business and its owner are separate. If the business pays the owner's household bills, that is drawings, not a business expense. Charging it to profit understates the profit. Pay ₹40 thousand of household bills. Compare profit with and without the mistake. Does the closing capital change with the mistake? Why?
narration.kn: ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಘಟಕ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆಯಂತೆ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಮತ್ತು ಮಾಲೀಕ ಬೇರೆ. ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಮಾಲೀಕರ ಮನೆಯ ಬಿಲ್ ಪಾವತಿಸಿದರೆ ಅದು ಸ್ವಂತ ಬಳಕೆ, ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ವೆಚ್ಚವಲ್ಲ. ಅದನ್ನು ಲಾಭದಿಂದ ಕಳೆದರೆ ಲಾಭ ಕಡಿಮೆ ತೋರುತ್ತದೆ. ₹40 ಸಾವಿರ ಮನೆ ಬಿಲ್ ಪಾವತಿಸಿ. ತಪ್ಪಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಲಾಭ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ. ತಪ್ಪಿನಿಂದ ಅಂತಿಮ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆಯೇ? ಏಕೆ?

title.en: On the board: Six basic concepts

say.en: Business entity: the firm is separate from its owner. Money measurement: only money events are recorded.
Going concern: the firm will continue, so assets stay at cost less depreciation.
Accounting period: one year, April to March. Cost: assets at the price paid.
Dual aspect: every transaction has two equal sides, so assets equal liabilities plus capital.
Suresh's machine: add freight and installation to the price. The dealer's offer is ignored.

prompt.en: Match each accounting concept with the practice it explains.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಲೆಕ್ಕಪತ್ರ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆಯನ್ನು ಅದು ವಿವರಿಸುವ ಆಚರಣೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ.

right.en: The owner's household bills are not recorded in the firm's books
The skill of the staff is not recorded, though it is valuable
Machinery is shown at cost less depreciation, not at its sale value
Profit is worked out for 1 April to 31 March
Land is recorded at the price paid plus registration charges
Every transaction affects at least two accounts equally

explanation.en: Each practice follows from one concept: separate entity, money measurement, going concern, accounting period, historical cost and dual aspect.

title.en: Accounting period, cost and dual aspect

body.en: Accounting period: the life of the business is divided into periods, usually one year (in India 1 April to 31 March), to measure profit and position regularly. Cost concept: assets are recorded at the price paid to acquire them, including expenses to bring them into use. Dual aspect: every transaction has two equal aspects, which gives the accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Capital.
body.kn: ಲೆಕ್ಕಾವಧಿ: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಒಂದು ವರ್ಷ (ಏಪ್ರಿಲ್ 1 ರಿಂದ ಮಾರ್ಚ್ 31). ವೆಚ್ಚ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆ: ಆಸ್ತಿಗಳನ್ನು ಕೊಂಡ ಬೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ದಾಖಲಿಸುವುದು. ದ್ವಿಮುಖ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆ: ಪ್ರತಿ ವ್ಯವಹಾರಕ್ಕೂ ಎರಡು ಸಮಾನ ಮುಖಗಳಿವೆ.

problem.en: Suresh bought a machine for ₹1,80,000, paid ₹8,000 freight and ₹12,000 for installation. A year later a dealer offers ₹2,50,000 for it. At what amount is the machine recorded, and which concept applies?

steps.en: The dealer's offer is ignored: under the cost concept (and going concern) the machine stays at cost less depreciation.
